functional_semantics.triton: output[j, i] = x[i, j] into a fresh (n, m) buffer of x's dtype, one read and one write per element (impl_triton.py 27-31, 48).
functional_semantics.cutile: output[j, i] = x[i, j] into a fresh (n, m) buffer of x's dtype, one read and one write per element (impl_cutile.py 25-26, 34).
functional_semantics.note: Both realise the reference x.transpose(0, 1).contiguous() (impl_torch.py 7) as a materialised out-of-place transpose.

stages.triton: One kernel over a 2-D grid of square tiles; each program loads an element tile with explicit strides and masks and stores the same values with row/column pointer arithmetic swapped, leaving any on-chip re-layout to the compiler (impl_triton.py 23-31).
stages.cutile: One kernel over a 2-D grid of square tiles; each CTA loads a 2-D tile, transposes it in registers with the DSL transpose primitive and stores it at swapped block coordinates (impl_cutile.py 25-26).
stages.note: Same single-stage tiled transpose; the difference is only the primitive used for the in-tile re-layout (address swap vs explicit tile transpose). The contract pins neither.

dependencies.triton: Tiles are independent; no inter-program dependency (impl_triton.py 20-31).
dependencies.cutile: Tiles are independent; no inter-CTA dependency (impl_cutile.py 23-26).

precision.triton: No arithmetic; bit-exact movement in the input dtype (impl_triton.py 28, 31).
precision.cutile: No arithmetic; bit-exact movement in the input dtype (impl_cutile.py 25-26).
precision.note: Same dtype in and out on both sides.

preprocessing.triton: Reads m, n = x.shape, allocates output (n, m), passes strides of x and output as kernel arguments (impl_triton.py 47-48, 54, 62).
preprocessing.cutile: Reads m, n = x.shape, allocates output (n, m), passes x as-is (impl_cutile.py 33-34, 56).
preprocessing.note: Only the output allocation; no copy, cast or re-layout of x on either side.

mutation.triton: x is read-only; fresh output every call (impl_triton.py 28, 48).
mutation.cutile: x is read-only; fresh output every call (impl_cutile.py 25, 34).
mutation.note: Neither side mutates the input; the contract forbids mutation.

hardware_dispatch.note: Single code path on both sides.

fq_boundary.note: Both timed run() bodies read m*n elements once and write m*n elements once with no preprocessing traffic and nothing prepacked, exactly what bytes_expr counts (config.yaml 18). flops_expr is 0 (config.yaml 17), so no compute intensity is defined; this is correct for a pure data-movement operator.
